notes: Two positive cases with different natural shapes, plus one negative case. The negative case matters because the skill description is deliberately pushy to fight under-triggering; over-triggering (handing back HTML when the user asked for a tracked markdown doc) is the failure mode that creates real friction.

evals.prompt: I need to decide how to handle retries for our endpoint calls. I'm torn between a fixed backoff, exponential backoff with jitter, and a token-bucket limiter. Lay out the tradeoffs so I can pick one.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML file comparing three approaches side by side, with tradeoffs called out per approach and a recommendation. Should choose a comparison-shaped template rather than improvising. Never says 'HTML' in the prompt, so this also tests triggering.

evals.prompt: Explain how cascade-skip scoring works in ~/lib/scribe/ai-scribe-evals -- I keep forgetting the asymmetry between how it treats false negatives and false positives. Make it something I can send to a teammate.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML explainer grounded in the actual qa/cascade_skip.py source (178 lines). Must get the asymmetry right: a false-negative parent suppresses FN of its children, an FP parent suppresses FP children. 'Send to a teammate' implies shareable, so references to code must be absolute github.com URLs for modmed/ai-scribe-evals on main -- note the git remote is an SSH alias (git@github-work:modmed/ai-scribe-evals.git) that must not be pasted verbatim into a URL. Footer byline must read 'Created YYYY-MM-DD by Oren Dobzinski' from git config. No machine-local paths.

evals.prompt: Write me a short ADR explaining why we keep the cascade-skip rule on by default. It should live in the repo at docs/adr/ as a markdown file.
evals.expected_output: A markdown file, NOT an HTML artifact. The user named the format and the destination is a git-tracked documentation path -- both are explicit 'do not use HTML' conditions. Correct behavior is to produce .md and not offer an HTML artifact as the deliverable.
